agent.problem: The rhetorical question and especially "Go ahead, idols, Papa Dorin will wait" already imply that no idol foretold these things. This rules out "True" on card 6 before the baker answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

agent.problem: The observation that this is the third call to listen uses verses 12 and 14 as well as verse 16, but the card cites only verse 16.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: The setup gives only the condition about paying attention to the commandments. It does not enable the baker to reason out the two poetic terms, so the blanks ask for wording from verse 18 that the baker has not seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: The callback to peace like a river uses verse 18, but the card cites only verse 22.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

human.problem: In Isaiah 48:16b, a speaker says 'the Lord GOD has sent me.' The card introduces this speaker only as 'a new voice.' The text doesn't name the speaker, and readers identify them differently (the prophet, or the Servant). Two rules point different ways here. papa-dorin.md says to name who is speaking before quoting someone who speaks as 'I.' The retelling rules say to leave open what the text leaves open.
human.question: When the text doesn't say who is speaking as 'I' and the speaker's identity is debated, should Papa Dorin name a speaker (for example, 'the prophet') or leave it open as 'a new voice'?
